chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who proposed to a man for his daughter from the free ones, so he came to him with another one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is returned to him, the one who was named for him, with another dower from her father, and the first dower is for the one with whom he had intercourse.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the dowry if a suitor changes the amount after proposing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of binding contractual terms in Shia jurisprudence, illustrating how a discrepancy between the agreed dowry and the actual provision allows for the bride's return with the original stipulation enforced by her father. It highlights the legal mechanism of 'mahr al-mithl' or adjusted compensation, ensuring the suitor fulfills the specific promise made during the proposal phase. The ruling underscores the importance of transparency in marriage contracts to prevent deception regarding financial obligations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who proposed to a man for a daughter of his from the free ones, so he came to him with another one. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would be returned to him, the one whom he had named with a dower from her father, and the dower is for the first one who he had copulated with’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who proposes marriage to a man for his daughter for a certain amount of mahr (dower) but he sends someone other than her. He (the Imam) said, ‘The one identified in marriage must be sent to him with mahr (dower) paid by her father and the mahr (dower) which was set first belongs to the woman with whom he has gone to bed.”’
